account: Today has seemed mostly routine. I read my appointments this morning, walked the plaza market around ten, bought fresh bread, and returned home for the noon lunch appointment. Residents I asked supplied no confirmed news. I am now at town hall, shortly after one, for the town accounts appointment. The one slightly unusual development is the secretary's effort to identify my afternoon tea host: she told me she checked dockside cottages, found them empty, and asked warehouse workers, who could not identify the host. This appears to have been ordinary preparation for my three o'clock appointment, not evidence of trouble. The neighbour personally confirmed at the plaza that tea is at the cottage at (16, -60, 105), beside the east ferry landing. I tried to tell the secretary this at home, but nobody was close enough to hear, so I should relay it again. The secretary is now visible inside town hall holding a writable book. I have no evidence of any other unusual activity or hidden purpose.
